title: Technical stub for platform partner onboarding v0.1
content:
Purpose:
A compact technical one-pager + speaker notes to help an SE run a 20–30 minute partner onboarding conversation focused on integrating Redwood Inference into a platform partner (SaaS or infra bundler). This is intentionally terse — use as a crib during calls and in early pilots.

TL;DR for SE:
- Goal: land a small pilot (1–2 endpoints, 1–2 models) with measurable latency and cost targets and a clear success metric (e.g., P99 < 400ms for 512-token gen, < 10x hosting cost target vs baseline).
- Ask early: Do you want hosted API (fast), dedicated pools (predictable), or private (VPC/on-prem)? Pick only one for pilot.

Audience: Solutions engineers, partner technical leads, product managers at partner orgs.

Core talking flow (20–30m):
1) Quick context (3m)
   - Partner product + intended inference surface (chat, summarization, embeddings, reranking).
   - If partner: user scale estimate (requests/min), median prompt size, expected tokens out.
2) Value props (3m)
   - Consistent, production-grade inference (latency SLOs, fallbacks).
   - Deployment flexibility: hosted, dedicated reserve, or private VPC.
   - Cost controls: batching, caching, quantization recommendations; we show unit economics.
3) Technical fit questions (8m) — script for SE:
   - "What's your expected steady QPS? Spikes?"
   - "Typical prompt length (tokens) and expected generation length?"
   - "Are you latency sensitive (P50 vs P95 vs P99)? Example SLO?"
   - "Data residency or encryption requirements? KMS/HSM?"
   - "Any offline/on-prem constraints or air-gapped needs?"
   - "Do you need model fine-tuning or can you use an off-the-shelf model?"

4) Architecture sketches (5m) — speak these, draw on whiteboard if possible:
   - Hosted flow: client -> Redwood API (multi-tenant) -> model variant -> streaming -> response.
   - Dedicated flow: client -> partner VPC peering -> reserved GPU pool -> autoscale config.
   - Private flow: customer VPC + control plane proxies -> on-prem runtime.
   - For all: optional prefix/KV caching layer, edge routing for region affinity, and fallback routing to lower-cost variants.

5) Pilot definition + success metrics (1–2m)
   - Start: 2 endpoints, one chat (gen) one embeddings. 2 weeks smoke + 4 weeks load/qual.
   - Success: P99 under target, throughput sustaining baseline QPS, < X tokens/sec cost threshold, quality regressions < 3% on evaluation set.

Common technical objections + suggested replies (short):
- "Latency unpredictable on hosted": we propose a canary on dedicated for baseline. Show historical P99 chart (sample).
- "Vendor lock-in": present model pinning & exportable KV/caching config; private deployment option.
- "Cost too high": run quick batching/caching sim, suggest quantized model variants and routing by policy.
- "Security/compliance": outline VPC + KMS support, audit logs, SOC/ISO artifacts (follow-up doc).

Quick scripts / soundbites for SE to use:
- "We can start hosted to validate features in under a day and migrate a subset of traffic to a dedicated pool for predictable tail latency."
- "If you need air-gapped, we have a private package and can run an initial security checklist in parallel with the pilot."

Integration checklist for a 2-week smoke pilot (practical):
- Account + API key exchanged.
- Sample integration app + sample prompts submitted to Redwood engineer.
- Model choice agreed (list candidate model IDs).
- Baseline perf run with partner sample prompts (collect P50/P95/P99).
- Define autoscale and burst policy for dedicated pool if chosen.
- KV/prefix cache policies decided (TTL, keys, footprint estimate).
- Instrumentation: tracing hook, token-level cost, and latency tagging enabled.

Data & metrics to gather during pilot (minimal):
- Request id, model_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, P50/P95/P99 latency, error categories, token cost per request.
- Qual evaluation: 100 labeled prompts run weekly, record human-rated quality delta.

Fallback & escalation playbook (short):
- If P99 > target for > 30m: route new requests to lower-cost variant + notify SE/Partner via channel.
- If errors spike > 5% for 10m: degrade features (reduce max_tokens, disable streaming), open incident.

Open questions to resolve before pilot kickoff (for SE to capture live):
- Which single production route will we test first? (chat / embed / rerank)
- Who is the engineering point of contact and slack channel?
- Expected billing cadence and approvals?
- Any compliance pre-reqs (IP whitelists, certs) to complete before demo?

Appendix: quick numbers (example) — replace with partner inputs on call:
- Example workload: 200 RPS sustained, average 256 prompt tokens, 128 completion tokens -> ~66k tokens/min.
- Rough hosted cost estimate: $X per 1M tokens (insert current pricing), rolling to dedicated can cut unit cost by ~30–60% depending on batchability.

Next steps (action items for SE at end of call):
- Share integration repo link + sample prompts by EOD.
- Schedule 30m tech kickoff with infra lead and product manager (within 3 business days).
- Productionize perf harness run and share baseline perf report within 5 business days.

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Bring sample P99 chart from last dedicated customer — good opener.
- Keep KMS explanation to 2 bullets; hand off compliance deep dive to security PM.
- If partner mentions LLM fine-tuning: collect dataset size, privacy needs; likely separate contract.

Version notes: v0.1 — lean crib for SEs, intended to be copied into call notes and iterated with partner-specific numbers.
summary: Crib for SE to run a partner onboarding pilot conversation: goals, probing questions, architecture sketches, objections, checklist, metrics, fallback playbook.
